lesson.title: Behaviorism and learning
lesson.summary: Behaviorism strengthened the controlled study of relations between the environment and behaviour. This lesson distinguishes its methodological project from learning mechanisms, then compares classical and operant conditioning while avoiding confusion between reinforcement, punishment, positive and negative.
objectives: Explain the methodological project of behaviorism and its historical context.
Represent classical conditioning with its stimuli and responses.
Analyse operant conditioning through a behaviour and its consequence.
Distinguish the experimental contribution, scope and limitations of a behaviorist explanation.
prerequisites: Distinguish observable behaviour from a mental process.
Understand the role of a measurement and an experimental condition.

content.text: At the beginning of the twentieth century, John B. Watson advocated a psychology centred on observable behaviour and relations between stimuli and responses. This project rejected private mental states as an indispensable basis for scientific explanation. It favoured operational definitions, controlled protocols and public predictions. Behaviorism was not a single doctrine, however: the positions of Watson, Skinner and contemporary learning research are not interchangeable.

In classical conditioning, an organism learns a relation between events. A stimulus that was initially neutral, when repeatedly paired with a stimulus that already elicits a response, may eventually trigger a conditioned response. The mechanism primarily concerns the predictive value of stimuli; it does not assume that the person voluntarily decides to produce the response.

In operant conditioning, the future probability of a behaviour varies according to its consequences. Reinforcement increases the behaviour; punishment decreases it. Positive means that an event is added and negative that it is removed. Negative reinforcement is therefore not punishment: it increases a behaviour because an aversive event disappears.

A revision app immediately congratulates a user after ten minutes of work and awards a point. If session frequency increases, the point or praise functions as positive reinforcement. If the user studies to stop an unpleasant alert and this strategy increases, removal of the alert may function as negative reinforcement. The category depends on the observed effect on behaviour, not the designer’s intention or whether the consequence seems morally pleasant.

Key point: behaviorist approaches produced powerful methods for studying learning and changing defined behaviours. On their own, they do not explain all human learning, especially when expectations, memory, observation of others, goals or social context alter behaviour. A useful explanation therefore states what the model predicts and what it leaves outside its scope.

concepts.title: The behaviorist project
concepts.description: Methodological behaviorism favours publicly observable relations between environment and behaviour, using testable definitions and predictions.

concepts.title: Classical conditioning
concepts.description: Classical conditioning describes learning a predictive relation between stimuli that changes an elicited response.

concepts.title: Operant conditioning
concepts.description: Operant conditioning describes how consequences change the future probability of a behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which objective does Watson place at the forefront of his manifesto?
questions.explanation: Watson presents an objective psychology aimed in particular at predicting and controlling behaviour.

questions.prompt: All authors described as behaviorists defend exactly the same theory.
questions.explanation: The term covers several historical and theoretical positions; Watson and Skinner are not interchangeable.

questions.prompt: Which elements correspond to the behaviorist methodological project?
questions.explanation: The approach favours measurable behaviour, public conditions and testable predictions.

options.label: Treat every private experience as sufficient evidence

questions.prompt: Which limitation should accompany a strictly behaviorist explanation?
questions.explanation: An analysis centred on contingencies may leave out relevant cognitive, social or biological processes.

options.label: It may omit internal processes and social context

questions.prompt: Which psychologist published Psychology as the Behaviorist Views It in 1913?
In classical conditioning, what does the organism mainly learn?
questions.explanation: It learns that one stimulus predicts another, which changes the response to the first.

options.label: A consequence following a voluntary action

questions.prompt: A conditioned response must necessarily be chosen voluntarily.
questions.explanation: Classical conditioning often concerns elicited responses that do not require a voluntary decision.

questions.prompt: After repeated pairings, a previously neutral sound elicits salivation. What has the sound become?
questions.explanation: The sound has become a conditioned stimulus capable of eliciting a conditioned response.

questions.prompt: Which elements must be identified in a complete classical-conditioning diagram?
questions.explanation: The diagram distinguishes stimuli and responses before and after learning.

questions.prompt: What is the initial phase during which the conditioned association forms called?

questions.explanation: Reinforcement increases the future probability of the behaviour it follows.

options.label: The person judges the consequence pleasant

questions.prompt: An alarm stops when a person fastens a seat belt, increasing seat-belt use. What is this?
questions.explanation: Removing the alarm increases the behaviour: this is negative reinforcement.

questions.prompt: In operant terminology, negative means bad or harmful.
questions.explanation: Negative indicates removal of an event; it is not a moral judgement.

questions.prompt: What information is needed to classify an operant consequence?
questions.explanation: You must determine what is added or removed and observe whether behaviour increases or decreases.

options.label: Is an event added or removed?
Does the behaviour increase or decrease?
Does the consequence seem morally good?
